entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 source 3196359642878570368: position at J2016.0. Distance: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19587: distance 37.313 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 37.313 +/- 0.448 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 26.1097 +/- 0.1777 mas (same row, RUWE 2.32), 146.9 standard errors, is not used. Proper motion: Gaia DR3 (same row): 10.233, 81.858 mas/yr. Radial velocity from SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3196359642878570368 (quality C), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none.

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 3.422 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19587: radius 3.422 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 25.536 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.036) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 7019 +/- 133 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19587: effective temperature 7019 +/- 133 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.03).

entries.subject: Color
entries.finding: Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 263: HR 1298; VizieR III/202, cross-checked against Gaia DR3 XP spectrum, source 3196359642878570368 (0 levels apart at most, the threshold is 12), through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #d9e1ff. Routes tried in order: stis-ngsl: HD 26574 is not in the library; pulkovo: HR 1298 is not in the catalogue; kiehling: HR 1298 is not among its 60 stars; burnashev: BS 1298 is not in part2; kharitonov: used.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 7,019 K and log g 3.39 (u1 0.320, u2 0.325): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. Gravity: log g 3.39 from 2003AJ....125.1598L; the 3 published values span log g 1.5 to 3.39, across which the limb law changes by at most 6.5% of the centre brightness.
